09 TakingYourTurn.ability:
TAKING YOUR TURN

It’s time to put your creatures to use!
Every creature gets one ACTION when their turn starts. The action can be used to ATTACK, MINE, or to put the creature into DEFENSE MODE.

ATTACK

A creature can choose any creature on the playing field to ATTACK. Attacking removes HP from the chosen creature equal to the ATTACK VALUE of the attacking creature, minus the DEFENSE VALUE of the creature being attacked. (See “ATTACKING” for more info)

A creature can choose any creature on the playing field to ATTACK. Attacking removes HP from the chosen creature equal to the ATTACK VALUE of the attacking creature, minus the DEFENSE VALUE of the creature being attacked. (See “ATTACKING” for more info)

MINING

A creature can choose to MINE, generating BRICKS equal to its STAR LEVEL for the player (see FIELD ITEMS for more)

DEFENSE MODE

A creature can use its action to go into DEFENSE MODE, doubling its defense while it is in this state. It goes out of defense mode at the beginning of its next turn. This state is singified by turning the creature 90 degrees.

A creature can use its action to go into DEFENSE MODE, doubling its defense while it is in this state. It goes out of defense mode at the beginning of its next turn. This state is singified by turning the creature 90 degrees.

TURN PHASES

PHASE 1

After it has been decided which slot’s turn it is, (see: “The Global Turn”), the slots turn begins and (BOT) effects Activate.

PHASE 2

This is the main part of a turn.
- May use (OYT) abilities.
- May now use items from the hand.
- May now swap facedowns to and from the hand.
- May now buy from the shops, and shuffle the item shop.
- May use actions.
- May swap primary and secondary fields if no actions have been used. (See: “THE FIELD”)

PHASE 3

- (ENDT) effects activate.
- Can no longer do anything you could in phase 2.

PHASE 4

The turn is now over.
- Status Effects deal damage/heal, duration ticks down by 1.

10 Attacking2.ability:
ATTACKING 2

MULTI-HIT ATTACKS

- Multi-hit attacks count as seperate attacks for each hit, and each instance may be reacted to seperately.
- When a creature uses an ability or item to attack multiple enemy creatures at once, the attacks happen left-to-right from the attacker's perspective and counter damage or on death effects both happen after all instances of the attack are resolved.

REDIRECTIONS

- Redirections & Interceptions, are instances where an attack’s target may be forecfully changed.
- Redirections change the attack’s target to a creature of choice.
- Interceptions change the target of an attack to be the creature which is intercepting.
- When a creature moves to intercept an attack, it cancels (and stays out of) defense mode first.

INFLICTIONS

- If a creature attacks or is attacked, any debuffs or stat changes inflicted on offense or defense are inflicted before the attack strikes, allowing those effects to alter the result of the attack. 
- Inflictions that occur from a creatures’ attack cannot be separated from the attack itself, and cannot be independently Negated/Reflected/Redirected/Intercepted whereas separate inflictions (from items and non-on attack abilities) can be.

ROUNDING

In the case that damage isn’t a.5 multiple, damage rounds up, for example 3.25 DMG rounds to 3.5 DMG

ABILITIES
INTRODUCTION
- A card’s ability is the main chunk of text at the bottom half of a creature that describes the unique function of the card past its basic actions. 
- Most abilities are unique, but how and when they can be activated are held together and defined by abbrviations. (See: “Abbrviations”)
- A creature’s ability is only active while on the field.
WHEN ABILITES CAN BE USED
1
2
Although (OYT) and (AAT) do not often appear on their own, they are the basis of when an ability can activate.
1. This ability can activate “on your turn” (OYT). Meaning you have to wait until the creature with this ability’s turn to use it.
2. This ability can be used “at any time” meaning at any point you may use this. These are able to be use reactivley (See: REACTIONS). This ability can be used to heal a creature that is about to die from an attack reactively.
PASSIVES
Passive abilities are abilites that are in constant effect (WOF) “while the creature is on the field”. “(WOF)” is often only included when the ability effects other creatures as to signfy that it goes away when the creature extis the field.

11 Abilities6.ability:
ABILITIES 7

ABILITIES 6

In rare cases some abilities can conflict. If you happen to run into these, here’s what to do.

SAME TIME

- When multiple effects happen simultaneously, such as (BOGT)/(ENDGT)/conditional effects, the creature with higher SPD takes precedence.

- After conflicting creature effects go, the team with the highest cumulative SPD’s active items go, field items are determined in the same way.

- In case of a tie for any of these, use turn order tie breakers.

- If one team has conflicting active or field item effects on its own side, owner chooses order. (active items still go first).

- If multiple abilities conflict on a singular creature(such as multiple on death abilities), the owner may choose the order/which abilities activate.

CONFLICTION

- If both teams can set the value of the same thing, (such as setting the value of RNG outcomes), it remains random.

- In the case of multiple revives procing at the same time that set  HP to a specific amount, the HP is combined. (Cannot go above Max)
Example: Two Life shrooms would revive a creature with 10 HP.

- If two simultaneous effects have directly conflicting effects, such as reviving in your base form or a distinct revive form at the same time, the player can choose.
Example: Azamoth with lifeshroom can revive as Azamoth The Possessed, or in it’s base form as The Forgotten king, but it it chooses it’s baseform the life shroom will be wasted.

Here are some specfic common abilities in the game and some specifics about them.

Ability Copying/Stealing/Swapping

- Stolen/Swapped abilities refresh as brand new per creature, if the creature loses that ability then gains it back, it’s not reset but instead incremented by a turn.
- If a creature gains an on first summon ability (or if this is the first opportunity that an OFS ability can be procced), proc it now.

MISC

- Counters are specific to every creature. 
- Abilities that count damage dealt to creatures do not count overkill damage.

If a healing item is used to deal DMG, it is instead treated as an attack item, and vice versa.

PASSIVES

(WOF) Friendly creatures gain +1 DEF.
This creature attacks inflict Burning.

This creature is immune to Poison.
This creature has 2 innate actions.

Passive abilities are abilites that happen automatically, without the player actively choosing to use it.

REACTIONS 2
Here, the order of events are listed by number that they’re played in, which is the reverse of the order they actually happen, and nothing happens until plays stop being made reactively. 
1. Mighty pebble is thrown (5 DMG)
2. Toy Bonnie reacts to the pebble with it’s ability to gain 6 Hardened (3 DEF) to make the damage from the Pebble 2 instead of 5.
3. The enemy reacts with Metronome, to try to negate (turn off) Toy Bonnie’s ability before it can give itself defense, so that the pebble would do 5 damage.
4. The player reacts to Metronome with Stopwatch, negating the Metronome before it can negate Toy Bonnie.
Once both players stop reactively using items, they then resolve and all the effects take place. So here, the order of events is 4>3>2>1. Resulting in the Pebble only doing 2 damage.

Although reactions happen in reverse order, anything that deals damage resolves last. Meaning all other effects take place before damage is dealt. Attacks also resolve forward, meaning the first damage item played resolves first.
1. The Mighty Pebble is thrown by the enemy (5 DMG).
2. Toy Bonnie uses it’s ability to give itself 5 stacks of hardened, giving it 3 defense. 
3. The enemy throws a bomb (7 DMG).
4. Toy Bonnie is equipped with metal sheild. (+1.5 DEF).
Now, the reaction chain is over. If their were no attacks, the order the plays resolve in would be 4>3>2>1, however since 2 of these do damage, the order of is actually 4>2>1>3.

ITEM TYPES 2

These item types do not get discarded immediately after played.

EQUIP

- These items you may equip onto your own creatures and grant a passive effect to the creature they are on which is lost when unequipped. 
- May be unequipped and returned to your hand during your turn.
- If an equip has a negative effect, cannot be unequipped until the start of the global turn after it was equipped. 
- If equipped creature dies, return equip to your hand. 
Equip’s stay equipped onto creatures swapped into the hand, and may be unequipped from creatures in your hand on your turn.
-Equip items may be equipped to an enemy if they have no negative effects, but the enemy would then own the item.
-An equip can be “Forcibly” unequipped by an effect at any time regardless of if the item has negative effects or is on cooldown. (Unless specified that it cannot be unequipped).

FRAGILE EQUIP

These items are same as equips but cannot be unequipped by any means and are discarded when the creature they are on dies. active ACTIVE

These items that stay on the field with a constant effect until they are destroyed. They have health and defense, although they are not creatures, cannot have items equipped to them, cannot have healing items used on them and cannot be inflicted with status effects. 15 Minions.ability:
MINIONS

INTRODUCTION

- Minions are small creatures that when summoned are attached onto a point-yielding parent creature.
- Minions are always attached to their parent creature, and stick with them even if the parent creature is moved or swapped into the hand.
- For most purposes, Minions are considered creatures, and have their own action, but they do not yield points on death. They do go to the graveyard on death.
- Every minion and parent creature in the primary field may use their actions (See: “THE FIELD”) in whatever order the player choses.
- Minions cannot mine for BRICKS.
- If Parent creature dies, all minions in the slot die (excluding persistent minions)

TYPES:Offensive minions occupy the same field as the summoner. (See: “FIELDS”):Protective Minions always occupy whatever field the parent creature and offensive minions are not in. When summoned, these push the parent creature (and the offensive minions attached to it) back to the secondary field, and are placed in the primary field. As a creature can only act in the primary field, This typically cannot act on the same turn as a parent creature, as they can never both occupy the primary field. (See: “THE FIELD”)
- If a protective minion is summoned after a parent creature has already used an action that turn, it does not gain an action for that turn.

PERSISTENT

If a minion is “persistent”, when it’s parent creature dies, it will be attached to the next point-yeilding creature that gets placed into the slot. If there is no creature to fill the slot, it occupies the slot alone, and must be killed for the game to be won by the opponent.

18 Field Cards.ability:
FIELD CARDS

These are cards that when on the playing field have a constant effect.

OBTAINING

- Field cards are cards that can be obtained from the Field shop, purchased with BRICKS. (See: “SHOPS”)
- Point-yielding creatures may spend an action to MINE, to generate an amount of BRICKS equal to their star level.

PLAYING

- When these are obtained, they may immediately be put into play on your teams field card slot, for no extra cost.
- You may take these out of play and put them in your hand. 
- If you want to put a field card from your hand into play, it’ll cost star points equal to the card’s star level, just like a regular item.
- You may have only 1 of these out at a time.

COUNTER-PLAY

- At the beginning of the global turn or on your turn, you may spend 1x the star level of a field item in BRICKS to negate it until the end of the global turn (field item stays on the field and can be swapped out, but loses its effect temporarily).
- Field cards can’t be negated on the same turn that they are played.
- Field cards cannot be negated 2 turns in a row
- At the beginning of the global turn, or on your turn, You may spend 3x the star level of a field card in BRICKS to destroy it.

STATUS EFFECTS
STATUS EFFECTS
- A status effect, is either a buff or debuff that has a an of effect on a creature, represented by Mr. Krabs either suffering or thriving.
- If a status effect deals DMG or Heals, then by default it procs at (ENDT). Otherwise, by the status effect take effect immediately.
- The duration of any status effect counts down at (ENDT).
This Panda was just inflcited with both 2 turns of Softened (-0.5 DEF), and 2 turns of Smouldering (2 DMG). Instantly, the DEF reduction takes effect. When Panda ends its next turn, it takes 2 damage from smouldering, and the duration for both of the debuffs goes from 2 to 1. 
SPECIFICS
- DMG dealing status effects count as one instance of damage per unique stack. (5 stacks of Poison is one instance of 5 damage.)
- Per unique status effect at (ENDT), the owner of the creature chooses the order in which to resolve these effects. (May chose if Regeneration heals before Smouldering does damage first)
- If a status effect deals DMG it is piercing, and doesn’t count as an attack.
- If a creature started the global turn with a status effect and the global turn ends without the creature having ended its turn, then the effect ticks at the end of the end of the global turn, even if the creature is in hand.

22 Negation.ability:
NEGATION

ATTACKS

If an attack is negated it does not happen. No damage is dealt, no on hit effects occour, The creatures does not get it’s action back, you do not pass go.

CREATURES

- When a creature is negated it is unable to use any of its own abilities (unless otherwise stated), but may still use the abilities of any equipped items or minions, and can still use actions.
- Multi turn based abilities such as (EOT) abilities count time passing even while they are negated.
- Minions/Items/Stats/Counters summoned/gained by an ability remain even if the ability that summoned them is negated or if the creature that summoned them dies. 
Immunity:
- 5+ star creatures are immune to negation.
- True Negation Immunity: Complete immunity to any possible sources of negation, including sources that negate negation-immune creatures.
- “On First Summon” abilities have true negation immunity.
- If an item/ability does something upon being negated, the “upon being negated” effect itself has true negation immunity

ITEMS

- If an item is negated, it means it cannot be played or is taken out of play, and it returns to the hand, (or back to being face down if it was denied play from a facedown slot.)
- If an item is negated or destroyed during use, the star points expended to use it are still expended.
- Items that are negated cannot be sold, or used for any other purpose until the negation ends.
- Equip and active items can be negated after their activation while they are still in effect, this sends them back to the hand, requiring star points to be used to reactivate them.

FIELD CARDS

- At the beginning of the global turn or on your turn, you may spend 1x the star level of a field item in BRICKS to negate it until the end of the global turn (field item stays on the field and can be swapped out, but loses its effect temporarily).
- Field cards can’t be negated on the same turn that they are played.
- Field cards cannot be negated 2 turns in a row
- At the beginning of the global turn, or on your turn, You may spend 3x the star level of a field card in BRICKS to destroy it.

Developper.ability: Precept One: 'Always Win Your Battles'. Losing a battle earns you nothing and teaches you nothing. Win your battles, or don't engage in them at all!     Precept Two: 'Never Let Them Laugh at You'. Fools laugh at everything, even at their superiors. But beware, laughter isn't harmless! Laughter spreads like a disease, and soon everyone is laughing at you. You need to strike at the source of this perverse merriment quickly to stop it from spreading.     Precept Three: 'Always Be Rested'. Fighting and adventuring take their toll on your body. When you rest, your body strengthens and repairs itself. The longer you rest, the stronger you become.     Precept Four: 'Forget Your Past'. The past is painful, and thinking about your past can only bring you misery. Think about something else instead, such as the future, or some food.     Precept Five: 'Strength Beats Strength'. Is your opponent strong? No matter! Simply overcome their strength with even more strength, and they'll soon be defeated.     Precept Six: 'Choose Your Own Fate'. Our elders teach that our fate is chosen for us before we are even born. I disagree.     Precept Seven: 'Mourn Not the Dead'. When we die, do things get better for us or worse? There's no way to tell, so we shouldn't bother mourning. Or celebrating for that matter.     Precept Eight: 'Travel Alone'. You can rely on nobody, and nobody will always be loyal. Therefore, nobody should be your constant companion.     Precept Nine: 'Keep Your Home Tidy'. Your home is where you keep your most prized possession - yourself. Therefore, you should make an effort to keep it nice and clean.     Precept Ten: 'Keep Your Weapon Sharp'. I make sure that my weapon, 'Life Ender', is kept well-sharpened at all times. This makes it much easier to cut things.     Precept Eleven: 'Mothers Will Always Betray You'. This Precept explains itself.     Precept Twelve: 'Keep Your Cloak Dry'. If your cloak gets wet, dry it as soon as you can. Wearing wet cloaks is unpleasant, and can lead to illness.     Precept Thirteen: 'Never Be Afraid'. Fear can only hold you back. Facing your fears can be a tremendous effort. Therefore, you should just not be afraid in the first place.     Precept Fourteen: 'Respect Your Superiors'. If someone is your superior in strength or intellect or both, you need to show them your respect. Don't ignore them or laugh at them.     Precept Fifteen: 'One Foe, One Blow'. You should only use a single blow to defeat an enemy. Any more is a waste. Also, by counting your blows as you fight, you'll know how many foes you've defeated.     Precept Sixteen: 'Don't Hesitate'. Once you've made a decision, carry it out and don't look back. You'll achieve much more this way.     Precept Seventeen: 'Believe In Your Strength'. Others may doubt you, but there's someone you can always trust. Yourself. Make sure to believe in your own strength, and you will never falter.     Precept Eighteen: 'Seek Truth in the Darkness'. This Precept also explains itself.     Precept Nineteen: 'If You Try, Succeed'. If you're going to attempt something, make sure you achieve it. If you do not succeed, then you have actually failed! Avoid this at all costs.     Precept Twenty: 'Speak Only the Truth'. When speaking to someone, it is courteous and also efficient to speak truthfully. Beware though that speaking truthfully may make you enemies. This is something you'll have to bear.     Precept Twenty-One: 'Be Aware of Your Surroundings'. Don't just walk along staring at the ground! You need to look up every so often, to make sure nothing takes you by surprise.     Precept Twenty-Two: 'Abandon the Nest'. As soon as I could, I left my birthplace and made my way out into the world. Do not linger in the nest. There is nothing for you there.     Precept Twenty-Three: 'Identify the Foe's Weak Point'. Every foe you encounter has a weak point, such as a crack in their shell or being asleep. You must constantly be alert and scrutinising your enemy to detect their weakness!     Precept Twenty-Four: 'Strike the Foe's Weak Point'. Once you have identified your foe's weak point as per the previous Precept, strike it. This will instantly destroy them.     Precept Twenty-Five: 'Protect Your Own Weak Point'. Be aware that your foe will try to identify your weak point, so you must protect it. The best protection? Never having a weak point in the first place.     Precept Twenty-Six: 'Don't Trust Your Reflection'. When peering at certain shining surfaces, you may see a copy of your own face. The face will mimic your movements and seems similar to your own, but I don't think it can be trusted.     Precept Twenty-Seven: 'Eat As Much As You Can'. When having a meal, eat as much as you possibly can. This gives you extra energy, and means you can eat less frequently.     Precept Twenty-Eight: 'Don't Peer Into the Darkness'. If you peer into the darkness and can't see anything for too long, your mind will start to linger over old memories. Memories are to be avoided, as per Precept Four.     Precept Twenty-Nine: 'Develop Your Sense of Direction'. It's easy to get lost when travelling through winding, twisting caverns. Having a good sense of direction is like having a magical map inside of your head. Very useful.     Precept Thirty: 'Never Accept a Promise'. Spurn the promises of others, as they are always broken. Promises of love or betrothal are to be avoided especially.     Precept Thirty-One: 'Disease Lives Inside of Dirt'. You'll get sick if you spend too much time in filthy places. If you are staying in someone else's home, demand the highest level of cleanliness from your host.     Precept Thirty-Two: 'Names Have Power'. Names have power, and so to name something is to grant it power. I myself named my nail 'Life Ender'. Do not steal the name I came up with! Invent your own!     Precept Thirty-Three: 'Show the Enemy No Respect'. Being gallant to your enemies is no virtue! If someone opposes you, they don't deserve respect or kindness or mercy.     Precept Thirty-Four: 'Don't Eat Immediately Before Sleeping'. This can cause restlessness and indigestion. It's just common sense.     Precept Thirty-Five: 'Up is Up, Down is Down'. If you fall over in the darkness, it can be easy to lose your bearing and forget which way is up. Keep this Precept in mind!     Precept Thirty-Six: 'Eggshells are brittle'. Once again, this Precept explains itself.     Precept Thirty-Seven: 'Borrow, But Do Not Lend'. If you lend and are repayed, you gain nothing. If you borrow but do not repay, you gain everything.     Precept Thirty-Eight: 'Beware the Mysterious Force'. A mysterious force bears down on us from above, pushing us downwards. If you spend too long in the air, the force will crush you against the ground and destroy you. Beware!     Precept Thirty-Nine: 'Eat Quickly and Drink Slowly'. Your body is a delicate thing and you must fuel it with great deliberation. Food must go in as fast as possible, but fluids at a slower rate.     Precept Forty: 'Obey No Law But Your Own'. Laws written by others may inconvenience you or be a burden. Let your own desires be the only law.     Precept Forty-One: 'Learn to Detect Lies'. When others speak, they usually lie. Scrutinise and question them relentlessly until they reveal their deceit.     Precept Forty-Two: 'Spend Geo When You Have It'. Some will cling onto their Geo, even taking it into the dirt with them when they die. It is better to spend it when you can, so you can enjoy various things in life.     Precept Forty-Three: 'Never Forgive'. If someone asks forgiveness of you, for instance a brother of yours, always deny it. That brother, or whoever it is, doesn't deserve such a thing.     Precept Forty-Four: 'You Can Not Breathe Water'. Water is refreshing, but if you try to breathe it you are in for a nasty shock.     Precept Forty-Five: 'One Thing Is Not Another'. This one should be obvious, but I've had others try to argue that one thing, which is clearly what it is and not something else, is actually some other thing, which it isn't. Stay on your guard!     Precept Forty-Six: 'The World is Smaller Than You Think'. When young, you tend to think that the world is vast, huge, gigantic. It's only natural. Unfortunately, it's actually quite a lot smaller than that. I can say this, now having travelled everywhere in the land.     Precept Forty-Seven: 'Make Your Own Weapon'. Only you know exactly what is needed in your weapon. I myself fashioned 'Life Ender' from shellwood at a young age. It has never failed me. Nor I it.     Precept Forty-Eight: 'Be Careful With Fire'. Fire is a type of hot spirit that dances about recklessly. It can warm you and provide light, but it will also singe your shell if it gets too close.     Precept Forty-Nine: 'Statues are Meaningless'. Do not honour them! No one has ever made a statue of you or I, so why should we pay them any attention?     Precept Fifty: 'Don't Linger on Mysteries'. Some things in this world appear to us as puzzles. Or enigmas. If the meaning behind something is not immediately evident though, don't waste any time thinking about it. Just move on.     Precept Fifty-One: 'Nothing is Harmless'. Given the chance, everything in this world will hurt you. Friends, foes, monsters, uneven paths. Be suspicious of them all.     Precept Fifty-Two: 'Beware the Jealousy of Fathers'. Fathers believe that because they created us we must serve them and never exceed their capabilities. If you wish to forge your own path, you must vanquish your father. Or simply abandon him.     Precept Fifty-Three: 'Do Not Steal the Desires of Others'. Every creature keeps their desires locked up inside of themselves. If you catch a glimpse of another's desires, resist the urge to claim them as your own. It will not lead you to happiness.     Precept Fifty-Four: 'If You Lock Something Away, Keep the Key'. Nothing should be locked away for ever, so hold onto your keys. You will eventually return and unlock everything you hid away.     Precept Fifty-Five: 'Bow to No-one'. There are those in this world who would impose their will on others. They claim ownership over your food, your land, your body, and even your thoughts! They have done nothing to earn these things. Never bow to them, and make sure to disobey their commands.     Precept Fifty-Six: 'Do Not Dream'. Dreams are dangerous things. Strange ideas, not your own, can worm their way into your mind. But if you resist those ideas, sickness will wrack your body! Best not to dream at all, like me.     Precept Fifty-Seven: 'Obey All Precepts'. Most importantly, you must commit all of these Precepts to memory and obey them all unfailingly. Including this one! Hmm. Have you truly listened to everything I've said? Let's start again and repeat the 'Fifty-Seven Precepts of Zote
